question: In a sanitary sewer collection system, what does the acronym CMOM stand for?
correctAnswer: Capacity, Management, Operations and Maintenance
explanation: CMOM stands for Capacity, Management, Operations and Maintenance. It is the US EPA framework for managing collection systems to reduce overflows.
options: Collection Monitoring and Overflow Measurement
Capacity, Management, Operations and Maintenance
Central Maintenance Operations Manual
Capacity Measurement and Outflow Modelling
optionA: Collection Monitoring and Overflow Measurement
optionB: Capacity, Management, Operations and Maintenance
optionC: Central Maintenance Operations Manual
optionD: Capacity Measurement and Outflow Modelling
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: CMOM Program Development.

question: What is the primary purpose of a CMOM program for a wastewater collection utility?
correctAnswer: To reduce sanitary sewer overflows through planned capacity, management, operations and maintenance
explanation: A CMOM program uses planned capacity assurance, management, operations and maintenance to prevent and reduce sanitary sewer overflows.
options: To eliminate the need for sewer cleaning
To replace all gravity sewers with force mains
To reduce sanitary sewer overflows through planned capacity, management, operations and maintenance
To transfer overflow response to property owners
optionA: To eliminate the need for sewer cleaning
optionB: To replace all gravity sewers with force mains
optionC: To reduce sanitary sewer overflows through planned capacity, management, operations and maintenance
optionD: To transfer overflow response to property owners

question: Which of the following is a core element of a documented CMOM program?
correctAnswer: Documented cleaning and inspection schedules with performance tracking
explanation: CMOM relies on documented, scheduled operations and maintenance activities, with records that let the utility track performance and improve the program.
options: Documented cleaning and inspection schedules with performance tracking
Responding only after a failure has been reported
Keeping no written records of overflows
Inspecting each sewer only once in its service life
optionA: Documented cleaning and inspection schedules with performance tracking
optionB: Responding only after a failure has been reported
optionC: Keeping no written records of overflows

question: Why does a CMOM program require the utility to record the cause and location of every sanitary sewer overflow?
correctAnswer: To identify recurring problem areas so corrective work can be prioritized
explanation: Overflow records show where and why overflows repeat. That pattern is used to prioritize cleaning, repair and capacity work where it will prevent the most overflows.
options: To assign blame to individual crew members
To meet a marketing requirement for the utility
To sell the data to neighbouring utilities
To identify recurring problem areas so corrective work can be prioritized
optionA: To assign blame to individual crew members
optionB: To meet a marketing requirement for the utility

question: Under the capacity assurance part of CMOM, what should a utility do before approving a large new development that adds flow to a trunk sewer?
correctAnswer: Evaluate whether the trunk sewer has adequate capacity for the added flow
explanation: Capacity assurance means evaluating system capacity before new flows are added, so growth does not create surcharging and overflows.
options: Evaluate whether the trunk sewer has adequate capacity for the added flow
Assume the trunk sewer will handle any added flow
Require the developer to operate the trunk sewer
Stop all cleaning on the trunk sewer for one year
optionA: Evaluate whether the trunk sewer has adequate capacity for the added flow
optionB: Assume the trunk sewer will handle any added flow
optionC: Require the developer to operate the trunk sewer
optionD: Stop all cleaning on the trunk sewer for one year

question: What is the main purpose of a sewer condition assessment program?
correctAnswer: To prioritize repair and rehabilitation using the actual condition and risk of each asset
explanation: Condition assessment collects inspection data on each asset so repair and rehabilitation can be prioritized by condition and risk, not by age alone.
options: To repaint all manholes on a fixed colour schedule
To remove the need for flow monitoring
To increase the design flow in every sewer

question: For condition data to be comparable between inspections and crews, assessments should be based on what?

A structured inspection method with consistent defect coding

question: In asset management for sewers, how is risk usually described?
correctAnswer: Likelihood of failure combined with the consequence of failure
explanation: Risk combines how likely an asset is to fail with how serious the failure would be. A poor condition sewer under a hospital or river crossing carries higher risk than the same sewer in an open field.
options: Pipe diameter multiplied by pipe length
Age of the pipe divided by its slope
Likelihood of failure combined with the consequence of failure
Number of manholes multiplied by depth
optionA: Pipe diameter multiplied by pipe length
optionB: Age of the pipe divided by its slope
optionC: Likelihood of failure combined with the consequence of failure
optionD: Number of manholes multiplied by depth

To train new staff on the camera equipment
To keep the camera contractor continuously employed

question: During CCTV coding, a structural defect is graded 5 on a 1 to 5 scale. What does that grade normally mean?
correctAnswer: The pipe has failed or is likely to fail soon and needs prompt action
explanation: On a 1 to 5 structural grading scale, grade 5 is the most severe category. It indicates failure or near failure, so prompt repair or rehabilitation planning is required.
options: The pipe has a minor cosmetic blemish only
The pipe is in like new condition
The pipe has failed or is likely to fail soon and needs prompt action
The defect is an operations issue with no structural effect
optionA: The pipe has a minor cosmetic blemish only

question: On a CCTV inspection, the operator sees a steady stream of clear water flowing into the sewer through a defective joint during dry weather. How should this be interpreted?
correctAnswer: As groundwater infiltration entering through the joint
explanation: Clear water entering through a joint or defect in dry weather is groundwater infiltration. A steady stream is recorded as a runner type infiltration observation.
options: As groundwater infiltration entering through the joint
As a root mass growing through the joint
As encrustation building up on the pipe wall
As a displaced joint with no water entry
optionA: As groundwater infiltration entering through the joint
optionB: As a root mass growing through the joint

question: Which of the following CCTV observations is a structural defect rather than an operations and maintenance defect?
correctAnswer: A longitudinal crack in the pipe wall
explanation: A longitudinal crack affects the pipe structure itself, so it is a structural defect. Grease, roots and settled debris affect operation and are maintenance defects.
options: Grease deposits on the pipe wall
A longitudinal crack in the pipe wall
Fine roots entering at a joint
Grit and debris settled in the invert

optionB: A longitudinal crack in the pipe wall
optionC: Fine roots entering at a joint

question: A CCTV report codes heavy roots at several joints in a clay sewer, with no cracks or deformation noted. What is the most appropriate first response?
correctAnswer: Schedule root cutting and, if regrowth is rapid, consider chemical root treatment or joint repair
explanation: Roots are a maintenance defect. Cutting removes the blockage risk, and rapid regrowth points to treatment or joint repair rather than full replacement when the pipe is otherwise sound.
options: Schedule root cutting and, if regrowth is rapid, consider chemical root treatment or joint repair
Immediately excavate and replace the entire sewer
Ignore the roots because they cause no operational effect
Line the sewer the same day without any cleaning
optionA: Schedule root cutting and, if regrowth is rapid, consider chemical root treatment or joint repair
optionB: Immediately excavate and replace the entire sewer
optionC: Ignore the roots because they cause no operational effect

question: A CCTV survey has to be abandoned partway because flow depth submerges the camera. What is the correct operator action?
correctAnswer: Record the survey as abandoned, note the reason, and arrange flow control or cleaning before a repeat survey
explanation: An abandoned survey must be documented with its reason. The uninspected length has no condition data, so flow control or cleaning and a repeat survey are needed to complete the assessment.
options: Code the uninspected length as being in good condition
Delete the survey and report the sewer as fully inspected
Record the survey as abandoned, note the reason, and arrange flow control or cleaning before a repeat survey
Grade all remaining defects as grade 5

optionB: Delete the survey and report the sewer as fully inspected

correctAnswer: The frame and cover, chimney, cone, wall, bench, channel and steps, plus evidence of inflow and infiltration

The frame and cover, chimney, cone, wall, bench, channel and steps, plus evidence of inflow and infiltration
Only the depth from rim to invert

question: Inside a manhole, the concrete crown and upper wall are soft, rough and losing material, while the bench below the flow line is sound. What is the most likely cause?
correctAnswer: Hydrogen sulfide corrosion above the flow line
explanation: Hydrogen sulfide released from sewage is converted to acid on moist surfaces above the flow line. That acid attacks concrete at the crown and upper wall, while submerged surfaces are largely protected.
options: Abrasion from grit in the flow
Freezing of ponded water on the bench
Hydrogen sulfide corrosion above the flow line
Damage from the cover being dropped
optionA: Abrasion from grit in the flow
optionB: Freezing of ponded water on the bench
optionC: Hydrogen sulfide corrosion above the flow line
optionD: Damage from the cover being dropped

question: What is the purpose of a chimney seal in a manhole?
correctAnswer: To seal the joint between the frame and the chimney against inflow
explanation: The chimney area between the frame and the cone is a common inflow path during wet weather. A chimney seal blocks that path and reduces rainfall dependent inflow.
options: To support traffic loads on the frame
To make the cover easier to remove
To seal the joint between the frame and the chimney against inflow
To anchor the manhole steps to the wall
optionA: To support traffic loads on the frame
optionB: To make the cover easier to remove
optionC: To seal the joint between the frame and the chimney against inflow

correctAnswer: Turbulence and debris accumulation that promote blockages and odours
explanation: A damaged bench and channel disrupt smooth flow through the manhole. The resulting turbulence drops solids, which build up, cause odours and can lead to blockages.

Higher pressure in the upstream force main
Lower groundwater levels around the manhole
Faster flow that cleans the upstream sewer

It prevents hydrogen sulfide from escaping, which is harmful
It increases the structural strength of the chimney

question: What is a cured in place pipe (CIPP) liner?
correctAnswer: A resin saturated flexible tube inserted into the host pipe and cured to form a new pipe inside it
explanation: CIPP uses a flexible, resin saturated tube that is inverted or pulled into the host pipe and then cured in place, forming a continuous new pipe within the old one.
options: A new rigid pipe pushed through the host pipe one joint at a time
A resin saturated flexible tube inserted into the host pipe and cured to form a new pipe inside it
A cement mortar sprayed onto the host pipe wall
A wrap applied to the outside of an excavated pipe
optionA: A new rigid pipe pushed through the host pipe one joint at a time
optionB: A resin saturated flexible tube inserted into the host pipe and cured to form a new pipe inside it
optionC: A cement mortar sprayed onto the host pipe wall

question: Before a CIPP liner is installed, what preparation of the host pipe is required?
correctAnswer: The host pipe is cleaned and inspected by CCTV so obstructions, dimensions and lateral locations are confirmed
explanation: Cleaning and a pre-lining CCTV inspection confirm the pipe is clear, correctly sized and mapped for laterals, which prevents a failed installation and blocked connections.
options: The host pipe is cleaned and inspected by CCTV so obstructions, dimensions and lateral locations are confirmed
The host pipe is pressurized to twice its normal flow
The host pipe is filled with grout along its full length
No preparation is needed because the liner fills every defect

question: Which methods are commonly used to cure a CIPP liner?
correctAnswer: Hot water, steam or ultraviolet light
explanation: CIPP resin is cured with heat from hot water or steam, or with ultraviolet light for UV cured systems. The cure schedule is controlled so the liner reaches its design strength.
options: Freezing, thawing and compaction
Hot water, steam or ultraviolet light
Chlorination and dechlorination
Sand blasting and painting
optionA: Freezing, thawing and compaction

correctAnswer: To keep sewage flowing for customers while the host pipe is taken out of service and kept controlled for lining
explanation: Lining requires the host pipe to be out of normal service. Bypass pumping carries the sewage around the work section so customers stay in service and the installation stays controlled.

To keep sewage flowing for customers while the host pipe is taken out of service and kept controlled for lining
To test the capacity of the downstream treatment plant
To wash resin out of the liner before curing

It removes the need for any inspection before or after
It increases the pipe diameter substantially

question: How does pipe bursting replace an existing sewer?
correctAnswer: A bursting head fractures the host pipe outward while pulling a new pipe into the same alignment
explanation: Pipe bursting pulls a bursting head through the host pipe, fracturing it outward into the soil while the new pipe is drawn in behind the head on the same alignment.
options: A bursting head fractures the host pipe outward while pulling a new pipe into the same alignment
A liner is inflated inside the host pipe and left soft
The host pipe is dissolved with chemicals and flushed away
A new pipe is tunnelled parallel to the host pipe and the host is abandoned
optionA: A bursting head fractures the host pipe outward while pulling a new pipe into the same alignment
optionB: A liner is inflated inside the host pipe and left soft
optionC: The host pipe is dissolved with chemicals and flushed away

By inserting a smaller new pipe into the host pipe and grouting the annular space between them
By bursting the host pipe and upsizing the diameter
By wrapping the outside of the pipe with steel bands
optionA: By spraying a thin coating that adds no structural strength
optionB: By inserting a smaller new pipe into the host pipe and grouting the annular space between them

The inserted pipe reduces the internal diameter, which can reduce capacity
It requires the sewer to flow under pressure at all times
It raises the invert so much that laterals cannot connect

question: A depth and velocity scattergraph from a flow monitor forms a loop that rises well above the normal curve during storms. What does that pattern most likely indicate?
correctAnswer: The site is surcharging, so depth rises without a matching increase in velocity
explanation: In surcharge, depth increases under backwater conditions while velocity does not rise in proportion. The loop above the normal depth velocity relationship is a classic surcharge signature.

The velocity sensor has been installed upside down
The site is surcharging, so depth rises without a matching increase in velocity
The basin has no rainfall dependent I and I

Rainfall never occurs during those hours
Pump stations are always off during those hours
Groundwater levels peak at exactly the same time every night

The colour coding used in the monitoring report

question: A monitor record shows flow beginning to rise within minutes of rainfall starting and falling soon after rain stops. What source type does that timing point to?

RDII is clear water, while groundwater infiltration is always coloured
There is no practical difference in a flow record
